obligation: Nevada Gaming Commission Regulation 5.260 (Cybersecurity)
basis: Applies to Nevada gaming licensees; the company holds no gaming license and has no Nevada venues. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: NIGC MICS: information technology
basis: Applies to tribal gaming operations conducting Class II gaming; the company runs no gaming

obligation: BSA/AML program for casinos
basis: Applies to casinos and card clubs with gross annual gaming revenue over $1 million; the company is neither

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (Level 1 merchant and Level 1 service provider)
citation: PCI SSC standard (contractual, not law); Visa Account Information Security program levels
basis: About 49 million own card transactions a year, Visa about 25 million (more than 6 million: Level 1 merchant); the payment service transmits about 15 million client orders, Visa about 7.8 million (more than 300,000: Level 1 service provider). The merchant agreement requires an annual ROC and AOC; the 2025 ROCs were Compliant. Not a designated entity (Appendix A3). Not law

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices, including data security)
basis: For-profit corporation; no size threshold. Applies to data security and to statements about pricing, ticket limits and privacy

obligation: COPPA Rule
basis: Websites and the app are general audience and account creation requires age 18 or older. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (live-event tickets)
basis: Live-event tickets are a covered good (464.1); effective 2025-05-12. Applies to every price display the company makes, including client templates it renders

obligation: ADA Title III ticketing rules
basis: Concert halls, stadiums and other places of exhibition or entertainment are places of public accommodation (28 CFR 36.104); the platform sells accessible seating and enforces purchase limits and pricing

obligation: BOTS Act
basis: The company is a ticket issuer whose security measures and posted limits the Act protects; its bot defense records are evidence for referrals

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over ERP and payroll are tested by the SOX program and not repeated here

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification and reasonable measures; worked example)
basis: Headquarters and 9 venues in Florida and patrons who reside there; the company is a covered entity for its own patrons and a third-party agent for client venues. Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification laws of other states
citation: Statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Patrons in all 50 states; notify under the law of each state of residence, using counsel's state matrix

obligation: State comprehensive consumer privacy laws
citation: Each state with a comprehensive privacy law where the company meets the thresholds (counsel's list)
basis: Patron data volumes exceed common thresholds; counsel keeps the state list

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: The company exceeds $1 billion in revenue but meets none of the three additional tests (applied in counsel's memo during the gap analysis)

obligation: State biometric privacy laws
citation: Statutes of the states where AI-005 would operate; Fla. Stat. 501.171 and 501.702 definitions (worked example)
basis: The facial recognition entry pilot processes face templates from gate cameras; counsel to confirm each venue state

obligation: HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules
basis: First aid at venues is provided by contracted ambulance services; the company is not a covered entity or business associate

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as pending. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: Federal contract clauses on covered telecommunications and Kaspersky products
basis: No federal contracts or subcontracts in the contract repository; recheck if one is signed

obligation: Sanctions screening before any extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer consent before any extortion payment

obligation: Acquirer merchant agreement and card brand rules
citation: Merchant agreement; Visa What To Do If Compromised
basis: Merchant agreement requires notice within 24 hours of a suspected card compromise; card brand duties apply as merchant and as service provider

obligation: Client and owner agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, notice and availability terms)
citation: SL-1 client agreements; SL-2 venue management agreements
basis: SL-1 clients receive 99.9% monthly availability, 72-hour incident notice, the PCI DSS written acknowledgment and a SOC 2 Type 2 report; SL-2 owners receive monthly reporting, settlement statements and 72-hour notice, and their auditors ask for a SOC 2 report
